description: Hurricane wind design and impact glazing required for hospitals in Georgia coastal counties
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — COASTAL WIND DESIGN: The proposed {occupancy} is located in a Georgia coastal county (Brantley, Brunswick MSA, Camden, Chatham, Glynn, Liberty, Long, or McIntosh county) subject to enhanced wind design requirements under GA DPH Rule 290-9-7 and the Georgia-adopted building code. Hospitals are Risk Category IV structures and must be designed for ASCE 7 wind loads appropriate for the coastal Georgia location, including wind-borne debris region requirements. The construction documents do not demonstrate compliance with the wind-borne debris region requirements; no impact-resistant glazing or approved protection system is specified for exterior glazing in the wind-borne debris zone. This deficiency must be corrected prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Perform a wind design analysis per ASCE 7 (current Georgia-adopted edition) for the site-specific location, using Risk Category IV importance factor; document the design wind speed from ASCE 7 wind maps and include the wind design parameters on the cover sheet.
2. Determine the wind-borne debris region boundary per ASCE 7 §26.12.3 based on the design wind speed at the project site; for areas within the wind-borne debris region, specify impact-resistant glazing products (tested per ASTM E1886/E1996, Miami-Dade NOA, or Florida Building Code product approval) for all exterior windows, doors, and skylights.
3. Provide a glazing schedule on the architectural drawings identifying the tested impact rating, product approval number, and installation requirements for all impact-resistant glazing units in the wind-borne debris zone.
4. Confirm that roof-to-wall and wall-to-foundation connections are designed for the ASCE 7 Risk Category IV wind uplift and lateral loads; include connection details and calculations in the structural drawings.

description: Emergency generator minimum 96-hour on-site fuel supply required for Georgia Category 1 healthcare facilities
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — EMERGENCY POWER / FUEL SUPPLY (96-HOUR): The electrical specifications and generator design documents for the proposed {occupancy} do not comply with GA DPH Rule 290-9-7-.13, which requires a minimum 96-hour on-site fuel supply for emergency generators at Georgia Category 1 healthcare facilities (hospitals). The submitted specifications indicate a fuel tank capacity providing less than 96 hours of generator operation at full rated load. This requirement exceeds the NFPA 110 minimum and is specific to Georgia-licensed hospitals. Revise the fuel storage system to provide the required 96-hour minimum supply and resubmit for GADPH review.
fix_template:
1. Calculate the fuel consumption rate (gallons per hour) for all emergency generators at full rated load; size the on-site fuel storage system to provide a minimum 96-hour supply at that rate and document the sizing calculation in the electrical design narrative.
2. Show on the electrical and mechanical/plumbing drawings the revised fuel tank configuration, secondary containment, fill connections, overflow protection, level gauges, and fuel transfer pump arrangement; specify tank standards per NFPA 30 and NFPA 110 Level 1.
3. Reference GA DPH Rule 290-9-7-.13 in the Division 26 electrical specifications for essential electrical systems, and confirm NFPA 110 Level 1 compliance for all system components.
4. Coordinate the fuel tank installation with Georgia EPD underground or above-ground storage tank registration requirements and local authority building permit requirements.

description: Georgia ASC operating rooms require minimum 200 SF clear floor area
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — ASC OPERATING ROOM MINIMUM SIZE: The floor plan for the proposed ambulatory surgical treatment center does not comply with GA DPH Rule 290-9-7.03, which requires a minimum 200 SF clear floor area per operating room in Georgia-licensed ambulatory surgical centers. The clear floor area must be measured from the interior face of finished walls, excluding any fixed casework, equipment recesses, scrub sink projections, or structural columns. The submitted floor plan indicates OR clear floor area(s) below this minimum. Provide dimensioned floor plans confirming compliance with the 200 SF minimum for each operating room.
fix_template:
1. Revise the operating room floor plan to provide a minimum 200 SF net clear floor area measured from the interior face of finished walls; confirm that fixed casework, equipment alcoves, column projections, and scrub sink enclosures are excluded from the net area measurement.
2. Provide an enlarged dimensioned plan for each OR with the net clear area calculation annotated; confirm that the surgical table, anesthesia zone, instrument back table, and surgical team circulation requirements can be accommodated within the revised layout.
3. Include a room schedule on the drawings listing each OR's gross area and net clear area; note the applicable GA DPH Rule reference for each room's minimum area compliance.
4. Confirm that HVAC supply and exhaust air quantities, room pressure relationships, and infection control requirements per ASHRAE 170 and GA DPH standards are maintained in the revised OR layout.

description: Written infection control construction plan required for renovation or construction in or adjacent to occupied licensed hospital areas
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL CONSTRUCTION PLAN: The construction document submittal for the proposed project in or adjacent to the occupied {occupancy} does not include a written infection control construction plan as required by GA DPH Rule 290-9-7-.13. The infection control plan must address physical barriers, HVAC isolation, construction traffic routing, and the specific infection control class level determined by an ICRA assessment. This plan must be available for review by DPH surveyors throughout the construction period. No infection control construction plan has been included in the current submittal. Provide this document prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Prepare a written infection control construction plan that includes an ICRA matrix identifying the construction activity type and patient risk group; determine the required ICRA class level and document the specific infection control measures required for each project phase.
2. Include in the plan: physical barrier specifications (type, height, and attachment), location of construction entry/exit points with tacky mat requirements, HEPA-filtered negative air machine requirements and monitoring protocols, and restrictions on construction activities during specific patient care hours.
3. Show on the construction drawings (phasing plan or separate ICRA barrier plan sheet) the locations of construction containment barriers, HVAC isolation points, and construction traffic routes that avoid active patient care areas.
4. Identify in the plan the facility-designated infection control officer responsible for ongoing compliance monitoring; confirm the plan will be maintained on-site and made available to GA DPH surveyors upon request.

description: Georgia CON approval required before establishing new hospitals, adding beds, or major capital expenditures
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — CERTIFICATE OF NEED (CON): The proposed project for the {occupancy} appears to involve the establishment of a new hospital, the addition of licensed inpatient beds, or major capital expenditures that require a Certificate of Need (CON) from the Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH) under O.C.G.A. §31-6. CON approval must be obtained from the DCH Health Planning Division prior to initiation of GA DPH plan review. The current submittal does not include a CON approval letter or a DCH determination that the project is exempt from CON review. Provide this documentation before GA DPH plan review can proceed.
fix_template:
1. Determine whether the proposed project requires CON under O.C.G.A. §31-6 and the DCH Certificate of Need Program rules by evaluating the project against applicable thresholds (new hospital establishment, addition of licensed beds, capital expenditure thresholds for CON review).
2. If CON is required, submit a CON application to the Georgia Department of Community Health Health Planning Division and obtain a CON approval letter before submitting construction documents to GA DPH.
3. If the project is below the CON threshold or otherwise exempt, obtain a written exemption determination from the DCH Health Planning Division and include it in the GA DPH construction document submittal.
4. Include the CON approval letter or exemption determination as the first document in the GA DPH plan review submittal package; DPH plan review will not proceed for qualifying projects without this documentation.

description: Minimum 1 handwashing sink per 4 beds in open units; 1 per patient room in single-bed room configurations
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — HANDWASHING SINKS PER PATIENT BEDS: The floor plan for the proposed {occupancy} does not demonstrate compliance with GA DPH Rule 290-9-7-.06, which requires a minimum of 1 handwashing sink per 4 patient beds in open nursing unit configurations, and 1 handwashing sink per patient room in single-bed room configurations. Review of the nursing unit floor plan indicates [insufficient handwashing sinks for the proposed bed count / patient rooms without dedicated handwashing sinks at the required ratio]. Handwashing sinks must be located for convenient use by clinical staff providing direct patient care. Revise the drawings to demonstrate compliance with this sink-to-bed ratio requirement.
fix_template:
1. Count the total patient beds in each nursing unit and verify that the number of conveniently located handwashing sinks equals at minimum 1 per 4 beds for open-bay configurations, or 1 per room for single-bed room configurations; document this calculation in the plumbing design narrative.
2. Show on the floor plan the location of each handwashing sink dedicated to patient care use; sinks must be located within or directly adjacent to patient care areas and not require passing through other patient spaces to reach.
3. Specify handwashing sinks with gooseneck faucets and wrist-blade or sensor-actuated handles (not hand-operated knobs) to prevent recontamination after handwashing; reference GA DPH Rule 290-9-7-.06 and CDC hand hygiene guidelines in the plumbing specifications.
4. Update the plumbing fixture count schedule to include all patient care handwashing sinks and confirm the final sink-to-bed ratio meets or exceeds the GA DPH minimum in the project compliance narrative.

description: Georgia State Minimum Standard Energy Code compliance and mechanical commissioning required for new licensed hospital construction
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — ENERGY CODE / MECHANICAL COMMISSIONING: The construction documents for the proposed {occupancy} do not include a Georgia State Minimum Standard Energy Code (GSMEC, based on ASHRAE 90.1) compliance certification or a mechanical commissioning plan. New licensed hospital construction in Georgia must comply with the GSMEC for HVAC, lighting, and building envelope systems, and mechanical commissioning is required for all new hospital construction. No energy compliance documentation (COMcheck equivalent or Georgia ENERGYSTAR equivalent) and no commissioning plan or commissioning authority identification have been included in the submittal. Provide these documents prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Complete and include Georgia State Minimum Standard Energy Code compliance documentation (COMcheck reports or equivalent energy compliance forms) for the HVAC system, lighting, and building envelope; confirm compliance with the current ASHRAE 90.1 edition as adopted by Georgia.
2. Identify in the specifications any areas where hospital HVAC requirements (pressurization, air change rates, humidity control per ASHRAE 170) may require energy code tradeoff or exception documentation; include any required exception narratives in the energy compliance documentation.
3. Identify an independent commissioning authority (CxA) qualified in healthcare HVAC commissioning; include a commissioning scope plan in the specifications defining pre-functional testing, functional performance testing, and final report requirements.
4. Submit the final mechanical commissioning report as a project closeout document to GA DPH; confirm that the commissioning report includes air balance results, pressure relationship verification for all critical spaces, and temperature/humidity setpoint confirmation.

description: GA DPH plan review submission required with site plan, floor plans, MEP plans, and equipment schedule for licensed hospital construction
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA DPH PLAN REVIEW SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: The construction document submittal for the proposed {occupancy} is incomplete and does not meet the requirements of GA DPH Rule 290-9-7 for licensed hospital construction. A complete DPH submittal must include: a completed DPH plan review application, a project site plan, full architectural floor plans, mechanical/HVAC plans, plumbing plans, electrical plans, fire protection plans, and a medical equipment schedule. The current submittal is missing one or more of these required elements. Resubmit with a complete package including all required drawing disciplines and the completed DPH application.
fix_template:
1. Complete the Georgia DPH Health Care Facility Regulation plan review application form and include it as the first item in the submittal package; ensure all fields are completed including facility license number, project scope description, estimated construction cost, and applicant contact information.
2. Assemble the complete construction document set per the GA DPH submittal checklist: site plan showing facility location and utility connections; architectural floor plans at minimum 1/8-inch scale; reflected ceiling plans; room schedule; mechanical HVAC plans and schedules; plumbing plans; electrical single-line diagram and lighting plans; fire protection plans; and project specifications.
3. Include a medical equipment schedule identifying major fixed equipment (imaging systems, surgical lights, sterilizers, medical gas outlets) with equipment room dimensions, structural loading requirements, electrical requirements, and rough-in dimensions.
4. Submit the complete package to the Georgia DPH Health Care Facility Regulation section and retain the DPH receipt of submission confirmation; plan review status inquiries can be directed to the DPH Healthcare Facility Regulation office.
